units.text: As I, Daniel, watched the vision, I sought to understand, and there stood opposite me someone with a human appearance.
I heard a human voice in the midst of Ulai, calling, “Gabriel, give that one understanding of the vision.” The man cried out and said, “The vision concerns that command.”
He came and stood beside where I stood. As he came, I was disturbed and fell upon my face. He said to me, “Understand, son of man, for this vision is still for an appointed hour.”
As he spoke with me, I fell asleep face down on the ground. He touched me and raised me on the spot,
and said to me, “Behold! I am reporting what will happen at the end of the wrath to the sons of your people; it will still remain until the hours of the appointed time of completion.
You shall make a lampstand of pure gold, of worked metal. Its stem, branches, bowls, knobs, and lilies shall be made from it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides, three from one side of the lampstand and three from the other.
There shall be three bowls shaped like little nuts, with a knob and lily on one branch. So it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the lampstand there shall be four bowls shaped like little nuts; on one branch shall be its knobs and lilies.
There shall be a knob under the two branches extending from it, and a knob under the four branches extending from it; so it shall be for the six branches extending from the lampstand.
Its knobs and branches shall be made from it, the whole worked from one piece of pure gold.
You shall make its seven lamps and set them on it, and they shall shine from one face.
You shall make its snuffer and supports of pure gold.
All these utensils shall be a talent of pure gold.
See that you make them according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”
In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to all the remnant of the people, saying:
Who among you saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? As though it did not exist before you.

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,
and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.
For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.
And I will shake all the nations, and the choice things of all the nations shall come; and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord Almighty.
The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, says the Lord Almighty.

For the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the Lord Almighty; in this place I will give peace, says the Lord Almighty, and peace of soul as a possession for everyone building to raise this sanctuary.”

In the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, in the second month, Zorobabel son of Salathiel, Iesous son of Iosedek, the rest of their brothers the priests and Levites, and all who had come from captivity to Jerusalem began. They set the Levites from twenty years old and upward over those doing the work in the Lord’s house.
Iesous and his sons and his brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, sons of Judah, stood over those doing the work in the house of God; also the sons of Enadad, their sons and their brothers the Levites.

They laid the foundation for building the Lord’s house, and the priests stood in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the Lord according to the directions of David king of Israel.

They answered in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord: “For it is good, for His mercy toward Israel endures for ever.” All the people sounded a great cry of praise to the Lord at the founding of the Lord’s house.

And the gold and silver vessels of God’s house that Nabouchodonosor took from the house in Jerusalem and carried to the king’s sanctuary—King Cyrus took them from the king’s sanctuary and gave them to Sasabasar, the treasury keeper in charge of the treasury,
and said to him, ‘Take all the vessels, go and place them in the house in Jerusalem, in their own place.’
Then that Sasabasar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now it has been built, but it has not been completed.’
At that time Anani the prophet came to Asa king of Judah and said, “Because you trusted in Syria’s king and did not trust in the Lord your God, Syria’s force has been saved from your hand.
Were not the Ethiopians and Libyans a great force, with confidence and exceedingly many horsemen? Yet because you trusted in the Lord, He handed them into your hands.
For the Lord’s eyes look throughout all the earth, to show strength in every heart that is whole toward Him. You have acted ignorantly in this; from now on there will be war with you.”

Behold, I am sending the many fishermen, says the Lord, and they will fish for them; and after these things I will send the many hunters, and they will hunt them on every mountain and hill and from the rocks’ openings.
Because My eyes are upon all their ways, and their wrongdoings were not hidden before My eyes.
And I will repay double their injustices and sins, for which they profaned My land with the corpses of their abominations and with their lawless acts, by which they offended against My inheritance.
You shall not steal. You shall not lie. No one shall defraud his neighbour.
And you shall not swear by My name for an unjust cause, and you shall not profane the name of your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain; for the Lord shall by no means hold him guiltless who takes His name in vain.

Cursed is the man who makes a graven and molten image, an abomination unto the Lord, the work of the hands of a craftsman, and sets it in a secret place. And all the people shall answer and say: So be it.
Cursed is he who dishonours his father or his mother. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who removes his neighbour’s boundaries. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who leads the blind astray in the way. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who perverts the judgment of the sojourner, and of the orphan, and of the widow. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife, for he has uncovered his father’s covering. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with any beast. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or of his mother. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law. And all the people shall say: So be it. Cursed is he who lies with his wife’s sister. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who strikes his neighbour treacherously. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent life. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Cursed is every man who does not continue in all the words of this law, to do them. And all the people shall say: So be it.
Of David. Bless the Lord, my soul. Lord my God, Thou hast become very great; Thou hast clothed Thyself in praise and dignity,
wrapping Thyself in light like a garment, stretching out heaven like a hide curtain;
He roofs His upper chambers in waters, makes clouds His means of ascent, and walks on the wings of winds.
He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a burning fire.

A quarter of you will be consumed by death; a quarter of you will perish by famine within you; a quarter of you I will scatter to every wind; and a quarter of you will fall by the sword around you, and I will draw a sword after them.
My wrath and My anger against them will be completed, and you will know that I, the Lord, have spoken in My jealousy when I complete My anger against them.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the doors of the Tent of Testimony and wash them with water.
Take the robes and clothe Aaron your brother with the full-length tunic, the shoulder-piece, and the oracle-piece. Fasten the oracle-piece to the shoulder-piece for him.
Put the headband on his head and the holy plate on the headband.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
When your days are fulfilled and you sleep with your fathers, I will raise up your offspring after you, one who will be from your body, and prepare his kingdom.
He shall build Me a house, and I will set his throne upright for ever.
I will be a Father unto him, and he shall be a son unto Me. I will not withdraw My mercy from him, as I withdrew it from those before you.
I will make him secure in My house and in his kingdom for ever, and his throne shall be set upright for ever.’”
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.
Lift your eyes around you and see your children gathered. Behold, all your sons have come from far away, and your daughters will be lifted upon shoulders.
Then you will see and fear and be astonished in heart, for the wealth of sea, nations, and peoples will turn toward you. There will come to you
herds of camels, and camels from Madiam and Gaipha will cover you. They will all come from Saba, bringing gold and carrying frankincense, and they will proclaim the Lord’s salvation as good news.
All Kedar’s sheep will gather to you, and Nabaioth’s rams will come to you. They will be offered acceptably upon My altar, and My house of prayer will be glorified.
Who are these flying like clouds and like doves with their young?
Islands waited for Me, and Tharsis ships among the first, to bring your children from far away, with silver and gold, because of the Lord’s holy name and because Israel’s Holy One is glorious.
Foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will attend you. For because of My anger I struck you, and because of mercy I loved you.
saying, ‘Why did we fast, and Thou didst not see? We humbled our lives, and Thou didst not notice?’ For on your fasting days you pursue your wishes and prod all those under your control.
If you fast for lawsuits and fights and strike a humble person with fists, why do you fast for Me as today, to make your voice heard in an outcry?

I did not choose this fast, or a day for a person to humble his life. Even if you bend your neck like a ring and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, you will not thereby call it an acceptable fast.

‘It is not such a fast that I chose,’ says the Lord. ‘Instead, loosen every bond of injustice, undo the strangling ties of coercive agreements, release the crushed, and tear up every unjust written contract.
Break your bread for the hungry and bring homeless poor people into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him; do not overlook those belonging to your own family.
Then your light will break out early, and your healings quickly rise. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and God’s glory will enfold you.
You shall appoint judges and recording officers for yourself in all your cities which the Lord your God gives you, according to your tribes; and they shall judge the people with righteous judgment.
They shall not pervert judgment, neither shall they show partiality, nor take a bribe; for bribes blind the eyes of the wise, and overthrow the words of the righteous.
You shall pursue justly that which is just, that you may live, and enter and inherit the land which the Lord your God gives you.
Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Correct your ways and your practices, and I will settle you in this place.
Do not put your confidence in yourselves on false words, because they will not benefit you at all when they say, ‘The Lord’s temple, the Lord’s temple it is.’
For if you truly correct your ways and practices and truly execute judgment between a man and his neighbor,
and do not oppress a newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow foreign gods to your own harm,
then I will settle you in this place, in the land I gave your fathers, from age to age.

“Thou didst testify to them to turn them back to Thy law, but they did not listen. Instead, they sinned against Thy commandments and judgments, which, if a person does them, that person will live by them. They presented a disobedient back, stiffened their necks and did not listen.
“Thou didst prolong Thy dealings with them for many years and testify to them by Thy Spirit through Thy prophets, but they did not give ear. Thou gavest them into the hand of the peoples of the land.
“In Thine abundant compassion Thou didst not make an end of them or abandon them, for Thou art mighty, merciful and compassionate.
Since I kept calling and you did not obey, and kept extending words and you paid no attention,
but you were making my counsels ineffective and disobeyed my reproofs,
therefore I too will laugh at your ruin and exult when destruction comes to you,
and when sudden tumult reaches you and overthrow arrives like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you, or when destruction comes to you.
For when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; evil people will seek me and will not find me,
for they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
nor did they want to attend to my counsels, but they were sneering at my reproofs.
Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.
